newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JOHNNIC DEAL UNAFFECTED BY TOYOTA SALE - NEC. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: JOHNNIC DEAL UNAFFECTED BY TOYOTA SALE - NEC. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd's (Johnnic) sale on Tuesday of its stake in Toyota South Africa Ltd would have no impact on Johnnic's purchase in August by a black consortium, the consortium's head said.
Japan's Toyota Motor Corp (TMC) announced earlier in the day that it would buy Johnnic's 27.8 percent stake in Toyota for 446 million rand (corrects from 456 million rand).

In August the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC), which groups 50 black economic interests, signed a landmark deal with Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd to buy the bulk of Anglo's 47.4 percent interest in Johnnic.
"No, it will not affect our purchase," said NEC chairman Wiseman Nkuhlu.
"It just means we have the flexibility as the money will now be in cash in Johnnic," Nkuhlu told Reuters on Tuesday.
Nkuhlu said talks between Johnnic and the TMC over the sale of the Toyota SA stake were already at an advanced stage when the NEC struck its deal with Anglo.
"The Toyota negotiations were at such an advanced stage it would not have been good for South Africa for us to say reverse the decision," Nkuhlu said.
Nkuhlu said the price paid for the Toyota stake was "fair".
Analysts said the deal had been priced at 40.30 rand a share, compared to a net asset value of 46 rand a share.
He said many benefits would flow from Toyota SA's link up with the Japanese manufacturer, most notably a boost for exports.
"It will be good for the motor industry if Toyota be allowed by the mother country to service markets outside South Africa. Toyota Japan would not allow that if it did not have a stake in Toyota SA."
The NEC's membership includes South Africa's largest black listed company New Africa Investments Ltd and several leading trade unions.

The NEC has until October 28 to conduct a due diligence investigation into the affairs of Johnnic during which time it will finalise the funding needed to buy the initial tranche, comprising at least 20 percent, of Johnnic shares.
